limits: Native 64-bit host. Warm filesystem caches; one build per binary.
C graph uses flat edges and a handwritten map; Dewy uses per-node arrays and an insertion-ordered map.
String equality uses separately allocated payloads; C uses pointer/length pairs and libc memcmp, Dewy uses runtime strings.
Kernel times exclude input generation; wall times include the complete process.
Thread CPU timing excludes descheduling, but CPU frequency and cache contention still matter.
A 2% timing resolution is not a per-stage slowdown budget; compare both references.
Bootstrap intervals are approximate; inconclusive results require an isolated recheck.
Passing measured budgets does not establish language completeness or universal C parity.

disposition: Rejected: less than 1% measured compilation gain; four runtime comparisons inconclusive. Compiler patch reverted.
assessment_policy: Per-workload C-or-better release medians; no universal runtime slowdown allowance.
